title: About how many leaves does a big mango tree have?
description: Farhan looks up at a mango tree in his village. The video counts the leaves on one branch and uses tens to reach the whole tree.
teaching_notes: One idea: leaves on one branch times the number of branches. Watch for children who drop the zeros and say sixty.

source: A branch has about 150 leaves and a tree has about 40 such b
video_script.why: The child has estimated a 5-digit count from a book and now estimates a 4-digit count from a tree.
video_script.substitution: Count leaves on a few branches, then use tens to reach all forty branches.
video_script.anchor: Farhan under a big mango tree in his village near Hyderabad
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu multiplies fifteen by four and says sixty. The numbers are one hundred and fifty and forty, so zeros are lost and sixty is far too small.
video_script.payoff_line: the tree has about six thousand leaves

final_answer.spoken: about six thousand leaves, a four digit number

maths_rules: one branch has about 150 leaves; the tree has about 40 such branches
40 branches are 10 times as many as 4 branches: 600 × 10 = 6,000 leaves
6,000 has 4 digits; a 4 digit number is from 1,000 to 9,999
slip: 15 × 4 = 60 drops the zero of 150 and the zero of 40; one branch alone has 150 leaves
your turn: 200 bricks a row, 60 rows: 200 × 60 = 12,000 bricks; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: leaves on one branch, then the number of branches. Wrong idea: lose the zeros. The mango tree stays in the anchor band; the branch blocks build on the stage.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the big tree sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a big mango tree; one branch is marked about 150 leaves; a marker reads about 40 such branches; an empty box asks about how many leaves

narration: <bookmark mark='m26'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m27'/>Farhan looks up at a big mango tree in his village near Hyderabad.
<bookmark mark='m28'/>One branch has about one hundred and fifty leaves.
<bookmark mark='m29'/>The tree has about forty such branches.
<bookmark mark='m30'/>About how many leaves does the tree have?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.m31: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m31'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a hint card in the working band: first four branches; then ten times as many; watch the zeros

marks.m32: the words a few branches first light up
marks.m33: the words watch the zeros light up

narration: <bookmark mark='m32'/>Count the leaves on a few branches first, not on the whole tree.
<bookmark mark='m33'/>Then think how many times bigger the whole tree is, and watch the zeros.
<bookmark mark='m34'/>Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows 15 × 4 = 60 leaves; the bubble is held beside one branch of 150 leaves; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.m36: the bubble is held beside the branch of 150 leaves
marks.m37: the zero of 150 and the zero of 40 are circled
marks.m38: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m35'/>Fifteen times four is sixty, so the tree has sixty leaves.
<bookmark mark='m36'/>Sixty is much too small, because one branch alone has one hundred and fifty leaves.
<bookmark mark='m37'/>Fifteen is only the front part of one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m38'/>The zeros matter, so we must bring them back.

beats.on_screen: four branch blocks of 150 leaves: 100 × 4 = 400, 50 × 4 = 200, together 600 leaves

marks.m39: four branch blocks appear, each marked 150 leaves

narration: <bookmark mark='m39'/>Take four branches first.
<bookmark mark='m40'/>One hundred leaves, four times, make four hundred.
<bookmark mark='m41'/>Fifty leaves, four times, make two hundred.
<bookmark mark='m42'/>Four hundred and two hundred make six hundred leaves on four branches.

beats.on_screen: the 4 branch block is repeated 10 times to fill 40 branches; the line 600 × 10 = 6,000 appears; the answer card reads about 6,000 leaves; 6,000 is split into four digits

marks.m43: the block of 4 branches is repeated ten times
marks.m45: the answer card about 6,000 leaves appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m43'/>Forty branches are ten times as many as four branches.
<bookmark mark='m44'/>Ten times six hundred is six thousand.
<bookmark mark='m45'/>The tree has about six thousand leaves.
<bookmark mark='m46'/>Six thousand has a six and three zeros, so it is a four digit number.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears; the line leaves on one branch, multiplied by the number of branches appears; then a new line: a wall with 200 bricks in a row and 60 rows, and an empty box

marks.m48: the wall line appears with an empty box

narration: <bookmark mark='m47'/>Take the part, multiply by the number of parts, and then count the digits.
<bookmark mark='m48'/>Your turn. A brick wall has about two hundred bricks in a row and sixty rows. About how many bricks are in it?
